title: Advanced Laboratory Techniques
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Science Laboratory Technology 300L curriculum: core bench techniques used across analytical labs -- weighing, volumetric measurement, extraction, filtration, centrifugation, chromatography fundamentals, sterilization, and good laboratory practice for accurate, reproducible results.

questions.question: Which type of balance is required for accurately weighing 5 mg of a reference standard for a calibration curve?
options: A top-loading balance readable to 0.01 g
An analytical balance readable to 0.0001 g (0.1 mg)
questions.correct_answer: An analytical balance readable to 0.0001 g (0.1 mg)
questions.explanation: Analytical balances resolve to 0.1 mg, giving acceptable relative error when weighing small masses such as 5 mg; coarser balances introduce unacceptable weighing error at this mass.

questions.question: In volumetric analysis, why is a volumetric pipette preferred over a graduated (measuring) pipette when preparing a standard solution?
options: It delivers a single fixed volume with higher precision and accuracy
It can measure any volume up to its maximum capacity
It does not need to be calibrated
questions.correct_answer: It delivers a single fixed volume with higher precision and accuracy
questions.explanation: Volumetric pipettes are calibrated to deliver one specific volume with very tight tolerance, giving better precision than reading a meniscus along a graduated scale.

questions.question: When reading the meniscus of an aqueous solution in a burette, the correct practice is to read the volume at:
options: The bottom of the meniscus at eye level
Either point, as long as it is consistent
The midpoint between top and bottom
questions.correct_answer: The bottom of the meniscus at eye level
questions.explanation: Water and most aqueous solutions form a concave meniscus; the bottom of the curve is read at eye level to avoid parallax error.

questions.question: A technologist needs to separate a precipitate from a solution where the particles are too fine for filter paper to retain efficiently. The most appropriate technique is:
questions.correct_answer: Centrifugation
questions.explanation: Centrifugation uses centrifugal force to sediment fine particles rapidly, separating them from the supernatant even when particle size is too small for effective filtration.

questions.question: Before starting a centrifuge run, why must sample tubes be balanced in pairs of equal mass across the rotor?
options: To make the machine run more quietly
To prevent rotor imbalance that can damage the bearings or cause the centrifuge to vibrate dangerously
To ensure both samples spin at different speeds
Balancing is only cosmetic and does not affect performance
questions.correct_answer: To prevent rotor imbalance that can damage the bearings or cause the centrifuge to vibrate dangerously
questions.explanation: An unbalanced rotor generates uneven centrifugal forces that stress the drive shaft and bearings and can cause the unit to vibrate violently or fail.

questions.question: Liquid-liquid extraction using a separating funnel relies primarily on which property of the two solvents?
questions.correct_answer: Immiscibility and differing densities
questions.explanation: Two immiscible solvents of different density form separate layers, allowing an analyte to be selectively partitioned into one layer and drained off from the other.

questions.question: In a separating funnel, after shaking a mixture of an aqueous layer and diethyl ether, which layer is normally on top?
options: The aqueous layer, because it is always denser
The ether layer, because diethyl ether is less dense than water
It cannot be predicted without testing
questions.correct_answer: The ether layer, because diethyl ether is less dense than water
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether has a lower density (~0.71 g/mL) than water (1.0 g/mL), so it forms the upper layer after the two immiscible liquids separate.

questions.question: Soxhlet extraction is most appropriate for which type of sample preparation?
options: Extracting fats or oils repeatedly and exhaustively from a solid matrix using a volatile solvent
Measuring the pH of a soil sample
Titrating an acid against a base
questions.correct_answer: Extracting fats or oils repeatedly and exhaustively from a solid matrix using a volatile solvent
questions.explanation: The Soxhlet apparatus continuously recycles condensed solvent through a solid sample, giving exhaustive extraction of lipids and similar analytes, e.g. fat content determination.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using filter paper folded into a fluted (fan) shape rather than a simple cone during gravity filtration?
options: It looks neater in the funnel
It increases the surface area and speeds up the rate of filtration
It prevents any liquid from passing through
questions.correct_answer: It increases the surface area and speeds up the rate of filtration
questions.explanation: Fluted filter paper exposes more surface area to the funnel wall and creates air channels, allowing faster gravity flow of the filtrate.

questions.question: Vacuum (suction) filtration using a Buchner funnel is preferred over gravity filtration when:
options: The precipitate is extremely fine and gravity filtration would be too slow
The sample volume is less than 1 mL
questions.correct_answer: The precipitate is extremely fine and gravity filtration would be too slow
questions.explanation: Applying vacuum increases the pressure differential across the filter, dramatically speeding filtration of fine precipitates that would clog or slow under gravity alone.

questions.question: In thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the retardation factor (Rf) is calculated as:
options: Distance travelled by solvent front divided by distance travelled by the compound
Distance travelled by the compound divided by distance travelled by the solvent front
Distance travelled by the compound multiplied by time
Distance from origin to the top of the plate only
questions.correct_answer: Distance travelled by the compound divided by distance travelled by the solvent front
questions.explanation: Rf is defined as the distance the spot migrates from the origin divided by the distance the solvent front migrates, both measured from the origin.

questions.question: In column chromatography, a more polar mobile phase will generally cause a polar analyte adsorbed on a silica stationary phase to:
options: Remain permanently fixed at the origin
questions.correct_answer: Move faster through the column
questions.explanation: A more polar mobile phase competes more effectively with the polar analyte for the polar stationary phase sites, reducing retention and speeding elution.

questions.question: Autoclaving glassware and media at 121°C for 15 minutes at 15 psi achieves sterilization primarily through:
options: Moist heat under pressure denaturing microbial proteins
questions.correct_answer: Moist heat under pressure denaturing microbial proteins
questions.explanation: Saturated steam under pressure raises the temperature above that achievable at atmospheric pressure, and moist heat efficiently denatures proteins and destroys spores.

questions.question: Which sterilization method is most suitable for heat-labile solutions such as antibiotic stock solutions?
options: Membrane filtration through a 0.22 µm filter
questions.correct_answer: Membrane filtration through a 0.22 µm filter
questions.explanation: Filtration through a 0.22 µm membrane physically removes bacteria without exposing heat-sensitive compounds to destructive temperatures.

questions.question: When preparing a 1:10 serial dilution of a stock solution, what volumes of stock and diluent are combined to make 10 mL of the diluted solution?
questions.correct_answer: 1 mL stock + 9 mL diluent
questions.explanation: A 1:10 dilution means 1 part stock in a total of 10 parts, so 1 mL of stock is combined with 9 mL of diluent to give 10 mL total.

questions.question: A stock solution has a concentration of 2.0 mol/L. What volume of this stock is needed to prepare 500 mL of a 0.1 mol/L working solution?
questions.correct_answer: 25 mL
questions.explanation: Using C1V1 = C2V2: V1 = (0.1 mol/L x 500 mL) / 2.0 mol/L = 25 mL.

questions.question: What mass of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) is required to prepare 250 mL of a 0.5 mol/L solution?
questions.explanation: Moles required = 0.5 mol/L x 0.250 L = 0.125 mol; mass = 0.125 mol x 40 g/mol = 5.0 g.

questions.question: Which piece of glassware gives the most accurate value when making up a solution to an exact final volume?
questions.correct_answer: Volumetric flask
questions.explanation: Volumetric flasks are calibrated 'to contain' a precise volume at a single graduation mark, giving the highest accuracy for making up solutions to volume.

questions.question: The term 'TD' (to deliver) marked on a pipette means the instrument:
options: Was calibrated to hold an exact volume when filled, without accounting for the film left on the walls
Is calibrated to dispense the stated volume, accounting for the residual film left inside after draining
Should never be used for aqueous solutions
questions.correct_answer: Is calibrated to dispense the stated volume, accounting for the residual film left inside after draining
questions.explanation: TD glassware is calibrated so that the stated volume is correctly delivered after normal draining, with the small residual film in the tip already accounted for -- it should not be blown out.

questions.question: Why should a hygroscopic reagent such as NaOH pellets be weighed quickly and not left exposed on the balance pan?
options: It absorbs atmospheric moisture, increasing its apparent mass and diluting the actual reagent content
It becomes radioactive on exposure to air
questions.correct_answer: It absorbs atmospheric moisture, increasing its apparent mass and diluting the actual reagent content
questions.explanation: Hygroscopic solids absorb water vapour from air, so prolonged exposure causes weight gain that is not the actual reagent, leading to inaccurate solution concentration.

questions.question: In gravimetric analysis, a precipitate is washed with a dilute electrolyte solution rather than pure distilled water mainly to:
options: Change the colour of the precipitate
Prevent peptization (colloidal dispersion) of the precipitate
questions.correct_answer: Prevent peptization (colloidal dispersion) of the precipitate
questions.explanation: Washing with pure water can cause some precipitates to disperse into colloidal particles (peptization) and pass through the filter; a dilute electrolyte wash minimizes this while still removing impurities.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of drying a precipitate to constant weight in gravimetric analysis?
options: To ensure all moisture/volatile matter is removed so the measured mass reflects only the analyte form
To make the precipitate easier to see
questions.correct_answer: To ensure all moisture/volatile matter is removed so the measured mass reflects only the analyte form
questions.explanation: Constant weight (unchanged mass on repeated weighing after further drying) confirms that all water and volatiles have been driven off, so subsequent calculations are accurate.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'accuracy' as distinct from 'precision' in laboratory measurement?
options: Accuracy is how close repeated results are to each other; precision is closeness to the true value
Accuracy is closeness of a result to the true or accepted value; precision is the reproducibility of repeated measurements
They are identical terms with no difference
Accuracy applies only to volumetric glassware
questions.correct_answer: Accuracy is closeness of a result to the true or accepted value; precision is the reproducibility of repeated measurements
questions.explanation: Accuracy reflects agreement with the true value, while precision reflects the spread/reproducibility among repeated measurements; a method can be precise but inaccurate, or vice versa.

questions.question: A technologist records a sample mass as 12.4560 g using a balance readable to 0.1 mg. How many significant figures does this recorded value have?
questions.explanation: 12.4560 has six significant figures: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 0 -- the trailing zero after the decimal point is significant because it reflects the balance's actual readability.

questions.question: Why must a light microscope's oil immersion (100x) objective be used with immersion oil rather than air?
options: Oil has a refractive index close to glass, reducing light refraction and improving resolution at high magnification
Oil prevents the slide from moving
Oil makes the specimen appear larger only, without affecting resolution
questions.correct_answer: Oil has a refractive index close to glass, reducing light refraction and improving resolution at high magnification
questions.explanation: Immersion oil matches the refractive index of glass, minimizing light bending between the slide and objective lens, which increases the numerical aperture and resolving power at 100x.

questions.question: What is the correct first step before using a compound light microscope to view a prepared slide?
options: Start on the highest power objective
Start on the lowest power objective and adjust coarse focus before moving to higher magnifications
questions.correct_answer: Start on the lowest power objective and adjust coarse focus before moving to higher magnifications
questions.explanation: Starting at low power gives a wide field of view for locating the specimen and reduces the risk of the objective striking the slide; focus is then refined at higher powers.

questions.question: A sample must be homogenized before analysis. What is the main reason for this step?
options: To ensure a representative, uniform sub-sample so analytical results reflect the whole sample
To change the sample's chemical identity
To reduce the total sample mass
questions.correct_answer: To ensure a representative, uniform sub-sample so analytical results reflect the whole sample
questions.explanation: Homogenization distributes components uniformly throughout the sample so that any aliquot taken for analysis is representative of the whole, reducing sampling error.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of steps for preparing a standard solution by dilution from a concentrated stock in a volumetric flask?
options: Add stock to the flask, fill exactly to the mark with distilled water first, then mix
Add stock to the flask, add diluent to roughly 90% of final volume, mix, then fill exactly to the calibration mark and mix again
Fill the flask completely with water, then add the stock last without mixing
Add stock directly to the graduation mark with no further dilution
questions.correct_answer: Add stock to the flask, add diluent to roughly 90% of final volume, mix, then fill exactly to the calibration mark and mix again
questions.explanation: Diluting to near-final volume before mixing avoids heat-of-mixing volume changes, and a final top-up to the calibration mark followed by mixing ensures an accurate, homogeneous solution.

questions.question: In laboratory record keeping, why should raw data be recorded directly into a bound logbook or LIMS rather than on loose scrap paper first?
options: Direct recording preserves data integrity, traceability, and prevents transcription errors or loss
It is faster to write on scrap paper
questions.correct_answer: Direct recording preserves data integrity, traceability, and prevents transcription errors or loss
questions.explanation: Good laboratory practice requires contemporaneous, traceable records; transcribing from scrap paper introduces the risk of transcription error and loss of the original data trail.

questions.question: A titration is repeated three times and gives concordant titre values within 0.1 mL of each other. This demonstrates:
questions.correct_answer: High precision of the technique
questions.explanation: Concordant (closely agreeing) repeat results indicate good reproducibility, i.e. precision; accuracy would additionally require comparison with a known true value.

questions.question: Which technique would best separate two miscible liquids with significantly different boiling points, such as ethanol and water?
questions.correct_answer: Simple distillation/fractional distillation
questions.explanation: Distillation separates miscible liquids based on differences in volatility (boiling point), vaporizing the lower-boiling component preferentially and condensing it separately.

questions.question: During a recrystallization purification, a hot saturated solution is cooled slowly rather than rapidly mainly to:
options: Allow larger, purer crystals to form by giving impurities time to remain in solution
Increase the solubility of the impurities permanently
questions.correct_answer: Allow larger, purer crystals to form by giving impurities time to remain in solution
questions.explanation: Slow cooling allows an ordered crystal lattice of the main compound to form while impurities, present in smaller amounts, tend to stay dissolved in the mother liquor.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a desiccator in laboratory technique?
options: To store hygroscopic materials or cooling crucibles in a moisture-free environment
questions.correct_answer: To store hygroscopic materials or cooling crucibles in a moisture-free environment
questions.explanation: A desiccator uses a drying agent (e.g. silica gel) to maintain a low-humidity atmosphere, preventing moisture uptake while a sample or crucible cools before weighing.
